gaps.sentence: The thief ran so fast that no one could ___ him.
gaps.hint: to capture someone who is running away
gaps.explanation: catch somebody means to capture or seize them after chasing.

gaps.sentence: The charity ___ over a million euros in a single weekend appeal.
gaps.explanation: 'Raise money' takes an object; rise/rose/arose are intransitive.

gaps.sentence: He ___ her a compliment on her new hairstyle.
gaps.explanation: pay somebody a compliment is the fixed collocation for praising someone.

gaps.sentence: The children ___ great fun at the party.
gaps.explanation: have fun / have great fun is the fixed collocation; 'made fun' means mocked someone.

gaps.sentence: After six hours of talks, the two sides finally ___ an agreement.
gaps.explanation: reach an agreement/decision is the collocation; 'arrive' would need 'at', which is not in the sentence.

gaps.sentence: She ___ very well in her end-of-year exams.
gaps.hint: collocation: to ___ well in an exam
gaps.explanation: do well in an exam is the standard phrase meaning to perform successfully.

gaps.sentence: It was three in the morning, but I was wide ___.
gaps.explanation: wide awake means completely awake; it is the fixed collocation with 'wide'.

gaps.sentence: The company ___ losses of two million last year.
